purpose: Preliminary form applicability only. A next result advances the questionnaire; it does not establish legal eligibility, approval, filing readiness, or permission to travel. Review results require current instructions and, where appropriate, qualified individual advice.
pdfVerificationMethod: Official USCIS URLs downloaded successfully on the checked date; pdfplumber/pdfminer confirmed an AcroForm field tree and Widget annotations. This verifies interactive PDF structure, not USCIS acceptance of an edition on a future filing date.

forms.scope: Report a noncitizen's change of U.S. address to USCIS; this is not an application for immigration status.

questions.text: Are you reporting a change of your U.S. address as a noncitizen?
questions.help: Answer for the person whose address is changing.
questions.stopReason: AR-11 is a noncitizen address-reporting form. Use USCIS address-change guidance to select the right process for a different purpose.

questions.text: Is your only purpose to change your address with an immigration court?
questions.help: AR-11 does not update the Immigration Court's records.
questions.stopReason: Use the court's separate address-change process. If USCIS also needs your new address, complete that update separately.

questions.text: Does your case require a protected or confidential address procedure?
questions.help: For example, special procedures may apply to certain abuse or trafficking survivor cases. Check USCIS guidance if unsure.
questions.reviewReason: Check the current USCIS instructions for your case type before entering or submitting a new address.

forms.scope: Optional email or text notice that USCIS accepted a paper filing at a Lockbox.

questions.text: Will you mail an application or petition to a USCIS Lockbox?
questions.help: This notice service is for Lockbox filings.
questions.stopReason: G-1145 is for acceptance notices for USCIS Lockbox filings. It is not a case-status inquiry or a separate immigration application.

questions.text: Do you want an email or text acceptance notice?
questions.help: You can request email, text, or both; overseas recipients receive email only.
questions.stopReason: G-1145 is optional. You do not need it if you do not want an electronic acceptance notice.

forms.scope: Request USCIS records under FOIA/Privacy Act, or an applicable Privacy Act record correction; no visa eligibility is assessed.

questions.text: Are you requesting USCIS-held records or an applicable Privacy Act record correction?
questions.help: Requests can concern your own records, another person's records, or USCIS agency records.
questions.stopReason: G-639 is a records-request form. Case-status inquiries, return of originals, and visa petition actions use other processes.

questions.text: Does the request include a living person's private records without their consent or evidence of your authority?
questions.help: Answer No for your own records or a request limited to agency records.
questions.reviewReason: Privacy protections can limit disclosure. Review USCIS consent, identity, and third-party request requirements before proceeding.

questions.text: Can you describe the records and provide enough information for USCIS to locate them?
questions.help: You do not have to know every field. Describe the documents or subject as clearly as you can.
questions.reviewReason: Clarify the records being requested; missing identifying information may prevent USCIS from locating them.

forms.scope: Supplemental information about the spouse beneficiary of Form I-130; filed with the spouse petition.

questions.text: Is this information for the spouse beneficiary of an I-130 petition?
questions.help: The beneficiary is the spouse seeking immigration through the petition; answer for that person.
questions.stopReason: I-130A supplements an I-130 spouse petition. It is not the supplement for a parent, child, or sibling petition.

questions.text: Is an I-130 spouse petition being prepared, or has USCIS requested this supplement for an existing petition?
questions.help: I-130A is not a standalone application for a green card.
questions.reviewReason: Confirm the related I-130 petition and when the supplement should be submitted.

questions.text: Can the required beneficiary information be completed and any required signature obtained?
questions.help: A spouse residing overseas must complete I-130A but does not have to sign it.
questions.reviewReason: Review missing information or the applicable signature instructions before submitting the supplement.

forms.scope: Select a travel-document, parole, re-parole, or parole-in-place request category; category-specific legal review is still required.

questions.text: Are you requesting a travel document, parole, re-parole, or parole in place?
questions.help: I-131 covers several different request types with different rules.
questions.stopReason: I-131 is for designated travel/parole requests, not a general passport, visa, or green-card renewal.

questions.text: Have you identified the I-131 request category that matches your situation?
questions.help: Examples include a reentry permit, refugee travel document, TPS travel authorization, or advance parole.
questions.reviewReason: Select the correct category and confirm its current requirements before preparing I-131.

questions.text: Are you already abroad, planning urgent travel, in removal proceedings, or unsure how travel affects a pending case?
questions.help: Travel rules and filing-location requirements vary by request type.
questions.reviewReason: Review the specific travel and case consequences before filing or departing. An I-131 filing does not itself authorize travel or guarantee return.

forms.researchNotes: Downloaded instruction PDF contains a draft watermark. Questions only address broad form purpose and direct category-specific uncertainty to review.

forms.scope: Carrier documentation for certain people abroad who lack documents needed to board transportation to the United States; not a replacement status document.

questions.text: Are you currently outside the United States and seeking to return?
questions.help: I-131A is used to request carrier documentation abroad.
questions.stopReason: I-131A is not the domestic replacement-document process. Check the appropriate replacement or travel form while inside the United States.

questions.text: Are you unable to board because your required return-travel document is missing, damaged, or otherwise unavailable?
questions.help: Some travelers can board with existing documents; the carrier and current guidance matter.
questions.reviewReason: Check whether carrier documentation is necessary before preparing or paying for I-131A.

questions.text: Are you a permanent resident, or did you hold a qualifying advance-parole document or EAD with travel endorsement?
questions.help: I-131A can cover certain non-residents with qualifying travel documents as well as permanent residents.
questions.reviewReason: Confirm the document category. I-131A is not an application for initial humanitarian parole.

questions.text: Can you document that your status or travel authorization remains valid and that your planned return meets its time limits?
questions.help: For residents, absences and reentry-permit validity matter; advance-parole travel authorization must still permit the return.
questions.reviewReason: An extended absence, expired/revoked authorization, or status concern requires case-specific review before requesting carrier documentation.

forms.scope: Financial support declaration for a specified temporary-stay or parole process that calls for I-134.

questions.text: Are you documenting financial support for a temporary U.S. stay or a parole request?
questions.help: Depending on the process, the person signing may support themselves or another beneficiary.
questions.stopReason: I-134 addresses temporary-stay financial support. Confirm the correct support form for a different immigration process.

questions.text: Does the relevant USCIS or consular process specifically request Form I-134?
questions.help: Support forms are not interchangeable; use the instructions for the beneficiary's process.
questions.reviewReason: Confirm that the current process calls for I-134 before preparing this declaration.

questions.text: Does the beneficiary's process require Form I-864 instead?
questions.help: I-864 is a different affidavit used in specified immigrant cases.
questions.stopReason: Use the required I-864 process. I-134 cannot replace an I-864 that the case requires.

questions.text: Can the person signing document access to the funds offered for support?
questions.help: Income, assets, dependents, and the length of support may be relevant.
questions.reviewReason: Review the financial evidence and the process-specific support requirements before signing.

forms.researchNotes: Downloaded instruction PDF contains a draft watermark. Confirm the current process and accepted instructions before filing; this check does not assess financial sufficiency.

forms.scope: Economic-need worksheet accompanying I-765 in deferred-action categories (c)(14) or (c)(33).

questions.text: Is your I-765 category (c)(14) deferred action or (c)(33) DACA?
questions.help: Check the category used for the employment-authorization request.
questions.stopReason: USCIS identifies I-765WS for categories (c)(14) and (c)(33). Other I-765 categories do not use this worksheet under these instructions.

questions.text: Are you preparing the related I-765 application?
questions.help: I-765WS is a worksheet, not a standalone request for employment authorization.
questions.reviewReason: Prepare or identify the related I-765 before completing its economic-need worksheet.

questions.text: Can you provide your own annual income, annual expenses, and current asset value?
questions.help: Use your own finances; the worksheet does not require other household members' financial information.
questions.reviewReason: Gather or reasonably explain your financial information before completing the worksheet.

forms.scope: TPS registration or re-registration; country designation, dates, court orders, and individual requirements need current review.

questions.text: Are you seeking Temporary Protected Status or TPS re-registration?
questions.help: DACA uses I-821D, which is a different form.
questions.stopReason: I-821 is for TPS. Select the form for your actual immigration request.

questions.text: Have you confirmed the current TPS rules for your nationality, or your last habitual residence if stateless?
questions.help: Check the USCIS country page; designations and related court orders can change.
questions.reviewReason: Review the current country-specific TPS guidance before assessing a filing path.

questions.text: Have you identified the applicable registration window and residence/presence dates, or a possible late-filing basis?
questions.help: Missing a standard filing window does not by itself resolve whether an exception is available.
questions.reviewReason: Registration dates, late-filing rules, and country-specific requirements need individual review; this check does not find you ineligible.

questions.text: Do you have any uncertainty about current TPS court orders, travel history, criminal history, or a prior decision?
questions.help: These issues can affect the available filing path.
questions.reviewReason: TPS requires a current country-specific and individual review before filing. This short check only identifies the form's purpose.

forms.researchNotes: Current TPS webpage retrieved directly. No fixed country eligibility or deadline is encoded. Downloaded instruction PDF contains a draft watermark.

forms.scope: DACA request or renewal; initial requests and renewal eligibility require current policy and individual review.

questions.text: Are you seeking consideration of DACA or a DACA renewal?
questions.help: This form is distinct from TPS Form I-821.
questions.stopReason: I-821D is for DACA. It is not a TPS application or a general request for immigration status.

questions.text: Have you previously received DACA?
questions.help: The current USCIS page says it processes renewals but does not process initial DACA requests.
questions.reviewReason: USCIS currently accepts but does not process initial DACA requests. Review current policy and your circumstances before preparing an initial request.

questions.text: Is your latest DACA period still valid or expired less than one year ago, and was it never terminated?
questions.help: A longer expiration gap or termination may require treatment as an initial request.
questions.reviewReason: Confirm whether USCIS treats this as a renewal or initial request, and how current court orders affect it.

questions.text: Have you had travel without advance parole, a break in continuous residence, a criminal case, or another change affecting DACA?
questions.help: Answering Yes does not establish ineligibility.
questions.reviewReason: Review current DACA rules, timing, and individual history before filing. I-765 and I-765WS accompany the DACA request.

forms.researchNotes: Current DACA webpage retrieved directly: renewals accepted/processed; initial requests accepted but not processed. Downloaded instruction PDF contains a draft watermark.

forms.scope: Contract to combine a qualifying household member's resources with an I-864 sponsor's resources; some intending-immigrant situations have exceptions.

questions.text: Will a household member's income or assets be combined with a sponsor's I-864?
questions.help: I-864A accompanies I-864 and is signed by the sponsor and qualifying household member.
questions.stopReason: I-864A is an attachment for combining qualifying resources with I-864. It is not a standalone affidavit or the usual form for a separate joint sponsor.

questions.text: Is the household member at least 18 years old?
questions.help: Answer for the person providing the household-member resources.
questions.stopReason: USCIS requires an I-864A household member to be at least 18. Review another qualifying support arrangement.

questions.text: Does the person meet the I-864A household-member or intending-immigrant rules?
questions.help: Qualifying relationships, principal residence, tax dependency, and intending-immigrant rules can differ.
questions.reviewReason: Review the household-member definition and any intending-immigrant exception before using I-864A.

questions.text: Is the resource contributor also the intending immigrant?
questions.help: An intending immigrant may not need I-864A, depending on dependents and whether income or only assets are used.
questions.reviewReason: Check whether I-864A is needed. The intending immigrant's income and assets have specific exceptions.

forms.scope: Replace or correct a previously issued naturalization/citizenship document, or request a special recognition certificate.

questions.text: Have you already been issued a citizenship/naturalization document, or are you a naturalized citizen seeking a special certificate for foreign recognition?
questions.help: Covered documents also include a Declaration of Intention or Repatriation Certificate.
questions.stopReason: N-565 is not the application to become a citizen or to obtain a first Certificate of Citizenship through a parent.

questions.text: Is the request for a lost/damaged document, an allowed correction or legal change, or a special recognition certificate?
questions.help: The supporting evidence depends on the reason selected.
questions.reviewReason: Confirm an N-565 filing reason in the current USCIS instructions.

questions.text: Are you requesting a change to information on the existing document?
questions.help: Name, date-of-birth, and other correction requests have different rules.
questions.reviewReason: Review the correction basis and evidence. USCIS cannot use N-565 to correct some information the applicant supplied and affirmed during naturalization.

forms.scope: Obtain a Certificate of Citizenship recognizing citizenship already acquired through a U.S. citizen parent; not adult naturalization.

questions.text: Are you claiming that you already acquired U.S. citizenship through a U.S. citizen parent?
questions.help: You can answer for yourself or a child; this form documents existing citizenship.
questions.stopReason: N-600 documents citizenship acquired through a parent. It is not the application for ordinary adult naturalization.

questions.text: Are you only replacing a lost, stolen, or damaged Certificate of Citizenship?
questions.help: Replacement of an existing certificate usually uses N-565.
questions.stopReason: Use the N-565 replacement-document process rather than a new N-600.

questions.text: Has USCIS already issued a decision on an N-600 for this person?
questions.help: A new N-600 is not the usual way to challenge a prior denial.
questions.reviewReason: Review the prior decision and available motion or appeal procedures before filing again.

questions.text: Has the applicable citizenship law and qualifying parent-child history been checked for this person?
questions.help: Dates, parentage, custody, residence, adoption, and some military/government-family rules can matter.
questions.reviewReason: Confirm whether citizenship was already acquired. A child living abroad may need a different process; current age alone does not determine the answer.
